paragraphs.title: A Plea for Protection and Deliverance from Pursuers

easy.explanation: He asks the LORD to plead his cause and fight against those who fight him.
easy.q: Whom does the psalmist ask to fight against his enemies?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “Take hold of shield and buckler.”
easy.q: What weapons of protection does the psalmist ask the LORD to take hold of?

easy.explanation: He asks the LORD to say, “I am thy salvation.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to say to his soul?

answers: They should return to help him
They should be confounded and put to shame
medium.explanation: He asks that they be turned back, confused, and put to shame.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask to happen to those who seek his soul?

answers: Light husks blown by the wind
medium.explanation: The enemies are compared to chaff driven before the wind.
medium.q: What does “chaff” refer to in this passage?

answers: Because the enemy hid a net for him without cause
Because the enemy asked him for help
Because he wants to use the trap himself
medium.explanation: The enemy secretly dug a pit and hid a net for the psalmist without cause.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask that the enemy fall into a trap?

answers: The enemies hide a trap, and the trap catches them
The enemies flee, and the psalmist pursues them
The psalmist sets a trap, and the enemies rescue him
challenge.explanation: The net hidden by the enemy catches the enemy himself.
challenge.q: What connection exists between verses 7 and 8?

challenge.explanation: His soul shall be joyful in the LORD and rejoice in his salvation.
challenge.q: What emotional result does salvation bring to the psalmist?

answers: As protector, defender, and deliverer of the poor
As one who asks the enemies for help
As one who remains distant from the events
challenge.explanation: The LORD fights the enemies and delivers the poor and needy from those stronger than they are.
challenge.q: How is the LORD’s role described throughout this passage?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “False witnesses did rise up.”
easy.q: Who rose up against the psalmist in verse 11?

easy.explanation: They rewarded him evil for good.
easy.q: What did the people repay the psalmist with instead of good?

answers: He prayed and fasted for them
easy.explanation: He wore sackcloth, humbled his soul with fasting, and prayed for them.
easy.q: How did the psalmist respond when his enemies were sick?

answers: Witnesses who accused him with lies
medium.explanation: They gave hostile and untrue testimony against the psalmist.
medium.q: What does “false witnesses” mean in this passage?

answers: He mourned for them, but they rejoiced at his trouble
He rejoiced at their sickness, but they prayed for him
He was silent, while they helped him
medium.explanation: He showed compassion when they were sick, but they rejoiced when he suffered.
medium.q: What contrast does the psalmist describe between his conduct and that of his enemies?

answers: They gathered together and rejoiced at his trouble
medium.explanation: They gathered against him, mocked him, and gnashed upon him with their teeth.
medium.q: What did the enemies do when the psalmist stumbled?

answers: He remained devoted to them despite their hostility
He was afraid of them and therefore stayed silent
He asked them to help him
challenge.explanation: His prayer, fasting, and mourning show compassion even toward those who mistreated him.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the psalmist’s praying for his enemies during their sickness?

answers: The psalmist helped them, but they repaid him with hostility
The enemies helped the psalmist, but he rejected them
The psalmist and his enemies treated each other kindly
challenge.explanation: He showed them kindness in their trouble, but they returned evil and mocked him.
challenge.q: How is the idea of evil in return for good shown in these verses?

answers: They did not stop their hostile actions
challenge.explanation: The enemies continued tearing at him without stopping.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “ceased not” emphasize about the enemies?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Rescue and Judgment

easy.explanation: He asks, “Rescue my soul from their destructions.”
easy.q: From what does the psalmist ask the LORD to rescue his soul?

answers: In the house of his enemies
easy.explanation: He promises, “I will give thee thanks in the great congregation.”
easy.q: Where does the psalmist promise to give thanks to the LORD?

easy.explanation: He asks that his enemies not rejoice over him wrongfully.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask his enemies not to do?

answers: The harmful attacks of his enemies
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks to be rescued from the destructive actions of his enemies.
medium.q: What does “their destructions” refer to in this context?

answers: So the LORD will see his trouble and act for him
So he can hide from the people
medium.explanation: He wants the LORD to intervene, rescue him, and judge his cause.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask the LORD not to keep silence or be far from him?

medium.explanation: The verse says they do not speak peace but devise deceitful matters.
medium.q: What do the enemies do instead of speaking peace?

answers: The psalmist asks both to be rescued from harm and to have the LORD judge his cause
The psalmist asks only to take revenge himself
The psalmist asks to leave the people without judgment
challenge.explanation: He asks for rescue from his enemies and for the LORD to judge his cause righteously.
challenge.q: How are the plea for rescue and the plea for judgment connected?

answers: They claim to have witnessed the psalmist’s downfall
challenge.explanation: The enemies speak as though they have seen the event they are celebrating.
challenge.q: What does “our eye hath seen it” reveal about the enemies’ words?

answers: The LORD should see, awaken, judge, and prevent the enemies’ rejoicing
The LORD should withdraw, remain silent, hide, and abandon judgment
The LORD should bless the enemies, and the psalmist should thank them
challenge.explanation: He asks the LORD to see, not keep silence, awaken to judgment, and judge according to righteousness.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the psalmist’s request in verses 22–24?

paragraphs.title: Shame for the Enemies and Joy for Those Who Love Justice

answers: They should be ashamed and brought to confusion
easy.explanation: He asks that they be clothed with shame and dishonour.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask to happen to those who rejoice at his hurt?

answers: Those who favour his righteous cause
easy.explanation: Those who favour his righteous cause are called to rejoice.
easy.q: Who should shout for joy and be glad?

easy.explanation: He says his tongue shall speak of the LORD’s righteousness and praise all day long.
easy.q: What will the psalmist’s tongue speak of all day long?

answers: Support or approve of his just cause
Have no interest in the judgment
medium.explanation: The phrase describes people who support the psalmist’s righteous cause.
medium.q: What does “favour my righteous cause” mean?

medium.explanation: They are told to say continually, “Let the LORD be magnified.”
medium.q: What will those who favour the psalmist’s cause say about the LORD?

answers: The enemies are ashamed, while the righteous rejoice and praise
The enemies rejoice, while the righteous remain silent
Everyone is ashamed and no one praises
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks for shame for his enemies and joy and praise for those who support righteousness.
medium.q: What is the main contrast at the end of the psalm?

answers: It describes the desired results of judgment: shame for the enemies and joy for the righteous
It cancels the request for judgment
It asks the enemies to become the judges
challenge.explanation: The final verses describe the outcome the psalmist desires after the LORD judges his cause.
challenge.q: How does the ending relate to the earlier requests for judgment?

answers: His thanksgiving and praise will continue continually
He will give thanks only once
He will stop speaking after deliverance
challenge.explanation: “All the day long” emphasizes continual and persistent praise.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the promise to speak of God’s righteousness “all the day long”?

answers: A community praises the LORD after justice is upheld
A community unites against the psalmist
challenge.explanation: Those who favour the righteous cause rejoice and magnify the LORD, joined by the psalmist’s praise.
challenge.q: What community picture is presented in the final verses?
